overview.description: Rainbow is a vibrant, strategic card game that focuses on completing a spectrum of colors while avoiding 'Clouds'. Players place cards into a shared central line to build a six-color rainbow. It is a game of careful hand management and risk assessment: if you add a duplicate color or a cloud card to the line, you are forced to collect all the cards currently on the table (which is bad for scoring). The winner is the player who collects the most 'Natural' rainbows or the fewest penalty cards, depending on the variant.
overview.deck: Specialized color deck (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet + Wilds/Clouds)

history.origins: Developed by Piatnik and other European manufacturers in the late 20th century as a 'Pure' color-focused alternative to number-heavy games like UNO.
timeline: 1990s: Piatnik releases the standard 'Rainbow' card game in Europe.
2010s: Becomes a popular educational tool for young children due to its visual mechanics.
Present: Maintained as a standard gateway game for families.
history.evolution: The game evolved from a simple matching game for toddlers into a more strategic hand-management game for adults, incorporating the 'Cloud' penalty system.
history.cultural: Used frequently in social play to emphasize 'Spectrum Completion' rather than zero-sum elimination.

setup.deck: 60-72 card specialized deck (6 colors x 10 cards + 6 Wilds + 6 Clouds).
setup.dealing: Each player starts with 6 cards. A central 'Rainbow Line' starts empty.

rules.objective: Complete 6-color rainbows to collect cards, or have the most cards at the end.
rules.gameplay: On your turn you play one card from your hand to the central Rainbow Line. The line builds toward a set of six different colors. If you play a card whose color is already in the line, or play a Cloud card, you must collect all cards currently in the line into your penalty pile. Wild cards can represent any color. The goal is to complete full rainbows to collect cards for points while minimizing penalty collections.
keyRules: Play one card per turn to the central Rainbow Line.
Duplicate color or a Cloud in the line forces you to collect all cards from the line as a penalty.
Complete six different colors in the line to form a Natural rainbow and collect those cards.
Wild cards count as any color; hold Wilds for the 5th or 6th slot when possible.
Winner has the most Natural rainbows or fewest penalty cards depending on variant.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the line! If the line already has Red, Yellow, and Blue, DO NOT play your Red card. If you only have Red, you are forced to take the penalty. Try to hold onto your 'Wild' cards for the 5th or 6th spot in the lineâ€”this is when you are most likely to complete a rainbow and take the points.
strategy.intermediate: Cloud Management: If the line has 4 cards in it, and you have a Cloud, use it! While it seems bad to take the cards, taking 4 cards is better than waiting and being forced to take 10 cards later. This is called 'Tactical Collection'â€”clearing the board so your opponent doesn't get a huge victory pile on the next move.
strategy.advanced: The 'Spectrum Trap': If you hold most of one color (e.g., you have 5 Greens), play your Green card early. This makes it very difficult for your opponents to complete a rainbow because you are hogging the green cards. They will be forced to play a duplicate or a cloud, allowing you to reset the line on your terms.
tips: If you have a hand of all the same color, you're in troubleâ€”try to cycle your cards as fast as possible.
A completed rainbow is worth 6 cards; a single penalty collection is often much more. Play for completion, not just shedding.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't notice duplicate colors in the line; plays Clouds too early; never completes sets.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable color tracking; uses Wilds strategically; basic tactical collection.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Card Hogging'; perfectly times Cloud clears to minimize penalties; calculates the probability of remaining colors in the deck.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
